newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court orders jail for anti-police rap singers.
newsitem.headline: French court orders jail for anti-police rap singers.

text.p: Two singers in a French rap band received three-month jail sentences and were banned from performing for six months for using lyrics savaging the police, justice officials said on Friday.

Bruno Lopez, also known as Kool Shen, and Didier Morville, called Joey Star, of the rap group NTM were also given additional three months' suspended sentences by a Toulon court on Thursday after being convicted of attacking public authorities through their songs.

Some left-wing groups decried the ruling as censorship. NTM stands for "Nique Ta Mere" (Fuck Your Mother). The public prosecutor had demanded they each be given a one-year jail sentence, part of it suspended.

Twenty-six policemen launched the legal action after they were on crowd control duty at a concert organised to protest against the election of a member of Jean-Marie Le Pen's far right National Front party as mayor of Toulon last year.
The court was told the group used the following lyrics during their performance in the Mediterranean city:

"I (sodomise) and piss on the courts. The police are the fascists and the murderers. It's those motherfuckers in blue and the courts who bust our balls all year round...our enemies are the men in blue (the police) and we piss on them."
Michel Blum, lawyer for Lopez, 30, and Morville, 29, neither of whom was in court, told Reuters they had appealed against the sentences, which put the penalties on hold.
The band has already won celebrity, and notoriety, with such song lyrics as "Kill the cops" and "Let's go to the presidential palace and kill all the old people".
One of their songs, "Fuck the police", describes police as "an organised gang, hierarchical, protected by the highest authorities".
The National Front has launched a campaign to prevent the group from performing at concerts and festivals which receive public funding.

Last June, after National Front leaders complained, prefect Jean-Charles Marchiani of the Var department in southeastern France put pressure on a festival near Toulon to cancel an NTM concert by threatening to withdraw subsidies.
The court ruling was applauded as an "excellent decision" by Francois Leotard, head of the centre-right Union for French Democracy (UDF) party who is a former culture minister.
"What creates problems are calls to hatred and violence...the magistrates were quite right to state that a minimum of social order must be respected because no country can live without it," he said.
But the Young Socialist movement described the sentences as "unaccceptable censorship and an attack on freedom of speech."
And the French Human Rights League described the ruling as an "unacceptable infringement of public freedom."
"Whether we like it or not, NTM is representative of what many youths express," said League president Henri Leclerc.
NTM, like similar groups in France, was created in imitation of black ghetto rap groups in the United States who have sometimes also run afoul the law because of their lyrics.

Many of the French groups are composed of youths of North African Arab or black African origin who live in depressed high rise suburbs outside main French cities plagued by unemployment, violence and drugs.
The two NTM singers are from one such area near Paris but both are white Frenchmen.
